Title: Opes Falsus Study #1
Text: Most of the life on this planet is fairly simple, but the violent lifeforms that resemble treasure chests - named opes falsus by previous expeditions - elude scientific explanation, including our own team’s efforts. Our team has managed to capture them on two separate occasions, but they’ve inexplicably gone missing, always leaving behind large mounds of solid waste. We plan to install cameras into our containment chambers to try and understand how this could be happening. What we have learned from the analysis we’ve done so far is that these lifeforms are much more genetically developed than the others. Their lineage may trace back millions of years.

Title: Opes Falsus Study #2
Text: Our team made a groundbreaking discovery yesterday. The “droppings” observed in the previous study were actually the opes falsus specimens themselves, somehow shifted into an entirely different physical form. Experiments have proven these aliens to be remarkably clever behind their vicious disposition - some of our interns are worried about them escaping into our headquarters and wreaking havoc. Fortunately, our containment procedures are sophisticated enough to keep these aliens in check and put those worries at ease.

Title: Opes Falsus Study #3
Text: The opes falsus species continues to amaze our researchers. Though they are quite aggressive, all complex organisms need sleep, and these specimens are no exception. Curiously, when at rest, the aliens retreat into the form of a featureless gray cube when they are dormant. We hypothesize that this is the “base” or “default” form of these aliens. The evolutionary purpose of this behavior is currently unclear. We ruled out camouflage as an explanation, as the cube, which appears almost manmade, does not blend in well with its natural surroundings.

Title: Opes Falsus Study #4
Text: I’m skipping the scientific talk. One of them escaped. None of us know how, but one of the opes falsus specimens is gone without a trace. We don’t know where it went. We’re all starting to worry, and for good reason. The alien might have just left for the outside world, but it could also be hiding anywhere in our facility, including in the escape pod, and given how savage these things are... it’s not looking good for us. We did find something else. We missed it the first time, we think it happened to be face down, but there’s a symbol on the aliens that appears when they sleep. It looks like a letter G with a helix pattern. We don’t know what this means, and we don’t have time to theorize. We have to find the escaped specimen.

Title: Gensis Inc. Announcement
Text: This is the announcement you’ve all been waiting for. Most of you are already familiar with our mission, so I’ll keep it brief. After years of work and several hundreds of experiments, we did it. Two hours ago, our scientists succeeded in creating a synthetic lifeform, one that can adapt like no other. This monumental achievement is the culmination of not just Genesis Inc., but the most brilliant minds of this world. Everyone, give yourselves a pat on the back - our mission has finally been accomplished.

Title: Lunacy Admin Log
Text: I can’t believe they pulled it off. Everyone said it would be a monumental undertaking. What they did, making it able to change shape too, should have been impossible. They’re taking all of the fame we deserve. But it doesn’t matter. The Lunacy Foundation’s crowning achievement will dwarf even that accomplishment. We just need a bit more progress. Our genius... MY genius... will not be cast aside.

Title: Chef's Notes
Text: I think I took a wrong turn going to Earth. The aliens here are aggressive and don't speak any language I know, but it turns out they still enjoy a good pizza. The treasure chest aliens will eat just about anything I give them, which works out great for getting rid of burnt pizzas. As for the others: basil for the cactus, olives for the eyeball, and, of course, mushrooms for the mushroom.

Title: Tattered Paper
Text: This is it. This is the end. I’m one of the last survivors. They fired me, called me mad for pointing out the cataclysm their mission would bring. But they stole our light from the night sky, and it’s ruined our world. Our ecosystem, everything we depend on, is in chaos. The oceans have grown stagnant and the nights are dark. This note is for you, Lunacy Foundation, when you return and see what your hubris has done. I hope you’re happy on your crazy lunar spaceship. You’ve doomed us all.
